message:
test(directory): count the retries, because the outcome does not

The 409 repair went in without a regression. Reading it, it is one retry;
the two ways it goes wrong are invisible in any suite that only checks
whether the connection worked. A client that retried forty times would pass
such a suite, and so would one that treated the refusal as a lost session
and signed out on the way to succeeding.

So this stands up a directory -- http and udp, in this process, on ports the
OS picks -- scripts the answers and counts the requests. The assertions are
counts:

  * a 409 on /api/connect is asked exactly twice, observed again in between,
    and never sends /api/login
  * a directory that refuses twice stops at two, not three or forever
  * a 404 is asked once: it is not repairable here, so it must not cost a
    second round trip

The host goes through HostAgent itself rather than a piece of it: register,
observe, heartbeat, and the 409 in the middle. Two heartbeats and exactly
one register -- the cached token survives, which is the whole point, since
dropping it is what makes an unattended PC need someone to walk to it. The
401 case is next to it as the contrast that gives that assertion meaning: a
401 IS the token being gone and does register again. If both statuses took
one path, the first test would pass for a client that treated every refusal
as a lost token.

directory_observe_from_health() had no test at all. It is the only place a
viewer that resumed from a stored session can learn where observations go,
and on https that answer decides between observing and refusing. Covered
here: the port, the host, a directory that says nothing (unknown, not an
error, and no invented port), a server error, and a server that is not
there.

One fix from writing it: the bootstrap left the first attempt's error text
in place after a successful retry, so a caller logging outError on success
would report a failure that had been repaired.
